Shri Vijay Sundaram - Govt. Advocate for respondent No. 2   ORDER

This Civil Revision has been filed against the order dated 23-11-2024, passed by II Civil Judge,
Junior Division, Raghogarh, Guna in RCSA No. 4/2024, thereby rejecting the application filed by applicant under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC.
2.

sentences.text:
The facts necessary for disposal of present civil revision in short are that, respondent No.
1/plaintiff has filed a suit for declaration of title as well as for permanent injunction against applicant and respondent No. 2 on the ground that plaintiff is the owner and in possession of agricultural land bearing Survey No. 51, area 1.348 hectares, situated in Patwari Halka No. 8, Tehsil Raghogarh, District Guna.
It is the case of plaintiff that aforesaid land has not been acquired by the State in accordance with law.
It was also claimed that the State Government has not transferred the aforesaid land to 2 CR-192-2025 applicant.
It has been further clarified by plaintiff that the State Government has neither acquired the land in a legal manner nor has paid the appropriate compensation amount to plaintiff.

It is further alleged that on 15-05-2023, employees of the applicant came to the land of plaintiff and, by claiming that the north-western part of the land belongs to applicant, started denying the title of plaintiff.
They also tried to interfere with the peaceful possession of the plaintiff.
It was further pleaded that name of the plaintiff has been removed from the revenue record.
Since applicant is denying the title of plaintiff, therefore, the suit has been filed for declaration of title and permanent injunction.

sentences.text: Applicant filed its written statement and claimed that the land in dispute was acquired by the State Government and an award was also passed on 30-08-1991, and compensation amount was also paid.
It was pleaded that applicant is the owner and in possession of the land in dispute from the date of acquisition, i.e., from 30-08-1991.
The plaintiff had never challenged the title of applicant in respect of Survey No. 51/1, area 0.052 hectare.
Name of the applicant is also recorded in the revenue records after 30-08-1991.

4. Applicant also filed an application under Section 9 read with Order 7 Rule 11 CPC for rejection of plaint on the ground that plaintiff has not disclosed any cause of action, and therefore, the plaint is liable to be rejected.

It was further pleaded that if the plaintiff is aggrieved by the insufficiency of compensation amount, then he should have made an application under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act seeking reference to the District Court.

The application was opposed by respondent No. 1.
6.

The trial Court, by impugned order dated 23-11-2024, has rejected the application filed under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC on the ground that plaintiff has not pleaded anything about the acquisition of land and he has merely filed a suit for declaration of title.

So far as the question of limitation is concerned, it was held that plaintiff has specifically pleaded that on 15-05- 2023, 4 to 5 employees of the applicant started denying the title of plaintiff, and therefore, it was held that prima facie the suit is within the period of limitation.
7.

Challenging the order passed by the trial Court, it is submitted by counsel for applicant that it is true that while deciding the application filed under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC, the Court is only required to look into the plaint averments.

However, it is submitted that this Court, in order to find out as to whether the suit is barred or not, can consider whether the plaint has been filed by cleverly drafting the same with an intention to give an illusory impression that the suit is not barred.
It is submitted that plaintiff has cleverly mentioned in paragraph 1 of the plaint that the suit land was not acquired in accordance with law and sufficient compensation has not been paid.
It is submitted that plaintiff should have challenged the acquisition proceedings.

So far as the insufficiency of compensation amount is concerned, it is the case of applicant that plaintiff had an alternative and efficacious remedy under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act and should have approached the District Court by filing an application for reference before the Collector.
8.
Per contra, counsel for respondent No. 1 has supported the findings 4 CR-192-2025 recorded by the court below.

9. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
10.

This Court has gone through paragraph 1 of the plaint, which reads as under:

sentences.text: 11. Counsel for respondent No. 1 was directed to clarify as to whether it is the case of plaintiff that the land has not been acquired at all, or it is his case that the land was not acquired in accordance with law and sufficient compensation amount was not paid.

12. Counsel for respondent No. 1 could not clarify the basic averment in paragraph 1 of the plaint and could not make a specific statement as to whether plaintiff has claimed that the acquisition proceedings were not done 5 CR-192-2025 in accordance with law, or it is his case that the land in dispute was never acquired by the State.

13. The Supreme Court in the case of Ramisetty Venkatanna and Another Vs. Nasyam Jamal Saheb and Others, decided on 28.04.2023 in Civil Appeal No. 2717/2023 has held as under:
"5.1 In the case of T. Arivandandam (supra) in paragraph 5 while considering the provision of Order VII Rule XI, this Court has observed as under: -
"5. We have not the slightest hesitation in condemning the petitioner for the gross abuse of the process of the court repeatedly and unrepentantly resorted to.

entities.text: Ramisetty Venkatanna and Another Vs. Nasyam Jamal Saheb and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From the statement of the facts found in the judgment of the High Court, it is perfectly plain that the suit now pending before the First Munsif's Court, Bangalore, is a flagrant misuse of the mercies of the law in receiving plaints.

The learned Munsif must remember that if on a meaningful -- not formal -- reading of the plaint it is manifestly vexatious, and meritless, in the sense of not disclosing a clear right to sue, he should exercise his power under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC taking care to see that the ground Gas Authority Of India Ltd. vs Man Singh Pindara on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8694520/
3 mentioned therein is fulfilled.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: And, if clever drafting has created the illusion of a cause of action, nip it in the bud at the first hearing by examining the party searchingly under Order 10 CPC.
An activist Judge is the answer to irresponsible law suits."

5.2 In the case of Sopan Sukhdeo Sable Vs. Charity Commr., (2004) 3 SCC 137 in paras 11 and 12,
this Court has observed and held as under:
"11.

entities.text: Sopan Sukhdeo Sable Vs. Charity Commr., (2004) 3 SCC 137
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In ITC Ltd. v. Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunal [ITC Ltd. v. Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunal, (1998) 2 SCC 70] it was held that the basic question to be decided while dealing with an application filed under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code is whether a real cause of action has been set out in the plaint or something purely illusory has been stated with a view to get out of Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code. 12.

entities.text: ITC Ltd. v. Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunal [ITC Ltd. v. Debts Recovery Appellate Tribunal, (1998) 2 SCC 70]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The trial court must remember that if on a meaningful and not formal reading of the plaint it is manifestly vexatious and meritless in the sense 6 CR-192-2025 of not disclosing a clear right to sue, it should exercise the power under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code taking care to see that the ground mentioned therein is fulfilled.
If clever drafting has created the illusion of a cause of action, it has to be nipped in the bud at the first hearing by examining the party searchingly under Order 10 of the Code.
(See T. Arivandandam v. T.V. Satyapal [(1977) 4 SCC 467].)"

entities.text: T. Arivandandam v. T.V. Satyapal [(1977) 4 SCC 467]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

5.3 In the case of Madanuri Sri Rama Chandra Murthy Vs. Syed Jalal, (2017) 13 SCC 174, this Court observed and held as under:
"7.

entities.text: Madanuri Sri Rama Chandra Murthy Vs. Syed Jalal, (2017) 13 SCC 174
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The plaint can be rejected under Order 7 Rule 11 if conditions enumerated in the said provision are fulfilled.
It is needless to observe that the power under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC can be exercised by the court at any stage of the suit.
The relevant facts which need to be looked into for deciding the application are the averments of the plaint only.

If on an entire and meaningful reading of the plaint, it is found that the suit is manifestly vexatious and meritless in the sense of not disclosing any right to sue, the court should exercise power under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC.

Since the power conferred on the court to terminate civil action at the threshold is drastic, the conditions enumerated under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC to the exercise of power of rejection of plaint have to be strictly adhered to.
The averments of the plaint have to be read as a whole to find out whether the averments disclose a cause of action or whether the suit is barred by any law.
It is needless to observe that the question as to whether the suit is barred by any law, would always depend upon the facts and circumstances of each case.
The averments in the written statement as well as the contentions of the defendant are wholly immaterial while considering the prayer of the defendant for rejection of the plaint.

Even when the allegations made in the plaint are taken to be correct as a whole on their face value, if they show that the suit is barred by any law, or do not disclose cause of action, the application for rejection of plaint can be entertained and the power under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC can be exercised.
If clever drafting of the plaint has created the illusion of a cause of action, the court will nip it in the bud at the earliest so that bogus litigation will end at the earlier stage."

sentences.text: In the case of Ram Singh Vs. Gram Panchayat Mehal Kalan, (1986) 4 SCC 364, this Court observed and held that when the suit is barred by any 7 CR-192-2025 law, the plaintiff cannot be allowed to circumvent that provision by means of clever drafting so as to avoid mention of those circumstances, by which the suit is barred by law of limitation.

entities.text: Ram Singh Vs. Gram Panchayat Mehal Kalan, (1986) 4 SCC 364
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similar view has been expressed by this Court in the case of Raj Narain Sarin (supra)."

Thus, it is clear that while deciding an application filed under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC, this Court can look into the plaint averments from an angle as to whether the drafting is a clever drafting made with an intention to give an illusory impression that the suit is not barred, or it is a clear drafting.

14. If the facts and circumstances of the case in hand are considered in the light of judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the case of Rami Setty Venkatanna (supra) , then it is clear that if intention of the plaintiff was to claim that land has not been acquired, then there was no need for him to claim in paragraph 1 of the plaint that the land was never acquired by the State Government in accordance with law, and no sufficient compensation amount was paid.

It should have been sufficient for the plaintiff to claim that he is the owner and in possession, and the property was never acquired, and the acquisition notification does not include the land in dispute.

Thus, it is clear that by cleverly drafting paragraph 1 of the plaint, in fact, the plaintiff is trying to challenge the acquisition proceedings by claiming that the acquisition proceedings were not done in accordance with law and sufficient compensation amount has not been paid.

15. Now the only question for consideration is as to whether the suit, thereby challenging the acquisition proceedings, is maintainable or not?
16.
Counsel for the applicant could not point out any provision from the Land Acquisition Act which bars the institution of a suit, thereby 8 CR-192-2025 challenging the acquisition proceedings.
17. If a land is acquired by the State, then the landholder has a remedy of assailing the said acquisition proceedings by filing a writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

Thus,
it is clear that the land acquisition proceedings are not beyond the scope of judicial review, and the plaintiff can always challenge the land acquisition proceedings on the limited grounds, like the land was not acquired for public purpose, or there is any inherent defect in the notifications, or the compensation amount was never paid at all etc. etc.
18.

If the plaint averments are seen, then it is clear that plaintiff has neither challenged the acquisition proceedings by pointing out as to how the acquisition proceedings were bad nor any relief has been claimed for quashment of the acquisition proceedings.

19. Thus, it is clear that plaintiff has cleverly drafted the plaint and although has mentioned in paragraph 1 of the plaint that the land was not acquired in accordance with law and adequate compensation has not been paid, but thereafter diverted the plaint towards the declaration of title.
If the land of the plaintiff has already been acquired, then it has stood vested in the State Government.
Without challenging the acquisition proceedings, plaintiff will not be able to seek declaration of his title.

It is a well-established principle of law that in absence of a consequential relief, a suit Gas Authority Of India Ltd. vs Man Singh Pindara on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8694520/
5 simpliciter for declaration of title is not maintainable.
20.

sentences.text: So far as the adequacy of compensation amount is concerned, plaintiff could have filed an application under Section 18 of the Land 9 CR-192-2025 Acquisition Act for reference of his case to the District Court for adjudication of adequacy of the compensation amount.
When a specific forum has been provided under the Land Acquisition Act, then the plaintiff should have availed the aforesaid statutory remedy.

21. Considering the totality of facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of considered opinion that the plaint, which has been filed by the plaintiff, is the outcome of clever drafting done with an intention to give an illusory impression that the suit is not barred under any law.

Furthermore, since the plaintiff has also not challenged the acquisition proceedings, therefore, no cause of action has arisen in favor of the plaintiff to file the suit for declaration of title and permanent injunction.
22.

Under these circumstances, this Court is of considered opinion that the plaint filed by plaintiff,
in its present form, is liable to be rejected under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC.
23.

Ex Consequenti, order dated 23-11-2024 passed by II Civil Judge, Junior Division, Raghogarh,
Guna in RCSA No. 4/2024 cannot be given the stamp of approval.

entities.text:
II Civil Judge, Junior Division, Raghogarh,
Guna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Accordingly, it is hereby set aside.

The plaint filed by respondent No. 1/plaintiff is hereby rejected under Order 7 Rule 11 CPC.
24.
The Civil Revision succeeds and is hereby allowed.
